proof_summary: Let \(m=\lfloor rn\rfloor\) and \(\alpha=rn-m\); irrationality gives \(0<\alpha<1\), while \(r^2=2r+\tfrac14\) yields \(a(n)=2m+K\) with \(K=\left\lfloor \tfrac n4+(2-r)\alpha\right\rfloor\), hence \(nr^2-a(n)=2\alpha+\tfrac n4-K\). Since \(-\tfrac14<(2-r)\alpha<0\), splitting according to \(n\bmod 4\) shows \(\tfrac14\le \tfrac n4-K\le1\); combining this with \(0<\alpha<1\) gives the two strict bounds.
